items.a: DevFest.cz 2026 takes place on 30 October 2026 at Uhelný Mlýn — a converted industrial mill in Libčice nad Vltavou, just outside Prague — fully in person. Registration opens at 8:00, the keynote starts at 9:00, and the day runs through the closing lightning talks into the afterparty. Capacity is strictly capped to keep the day focused, so grab a ticket early.

items.q: What does the day look like?
items.a: Registration opens at 8:00 (there is a cloakroom for coats and bags), kick-off is at 8:45, keynote at 9:00. From then on the talks run on two stages — Moonshine and Speakeasy — in 20- and 40-minute slots, with a lunch break around midday and a longer break in the afternoon. Lightning talks and closing remarks wrap up around 18:30, and the afterparty follows. The full timetable is on the agenda page; a slot or two may still shift.

items.q: How do I get to the venue?
items.a: Uhelný Mlýn is at Areál Šroubáren 860, 252 66 Libčice nad Vltavou — on the map it looks like a trip, in practice it is Prague's backyard: a direct train from the city centre gets you there in 25–30 minutes. Trains toward Kralupy nad Vltavou leave from Praha hlavní nádraží and Praha-Holešovice about every 30 minutes (they also call at Praha-Podbaba) — get off at Libčice nad Vltavou. From the station it is a 10-minute walk (about 0.7 km) to the venue.

items.q: I'm flying in — which airport, and where should I stay?
items.a: Fly to Prague (Václav Havel Airport, PRG) — the venue is just outside the city, not in another one. From the airport, trolleybus 59 to Nádraží Veleslavín and metro A take you into town in about 45 minutes; the Airport Express bus runs straight to Praha hlavní nádraží. Stay anywhere near Praha hlavní nádraží or Holešovice and the venue is a single 25–30-minute train ride away on the day.
It's run by GUG.cz, z.s. — a Czech developer community. DevFest.cz is a volunteer-driven community event, now in its 11th edition.

Tickets are sold in three waves — Early Bird, Regular, and Lazy Bird — with the price rising each wave. Early Bird has closed. Regular tickets are on sale until 30 September 2026: 2 999 Kč individual and 4 499 Kč company funded, VAT included. Lazy Bird follows. Live pricing for the current wave is always shown in the Tickets section on the home page.
Each wave offers two options: Individual (personal purchase) and Company funded (priced for employer-reimbursed purchases). Both grant full access to the conference — every talk on both stages.

Tickets are sold through ti.to from the Tickets section on the home page. Pay by card and the ticket lands in your inbox right away. Each wave closes on its date or when it sells out — the earlier you grab one, the better the price.

items.q: Can I get an invoice for my company?
items.a: Yes. Request one on the invoice page — we issue a proper invoice, you pay by bank transfer, and we send back a code that covers the tickets in full. If you can pay by card, ti.to emails a receipt the moment you buy.

The lineup is live on the speakers page — developers, Google Developer Experts and researchers from across Europe and beyond, with a few more names still to land. Every talk, with its abstract and speakers, is on the sessions page.

AI agents, generative UI, cloud & backends, mobile & web (accessibility included), and the humans in tech — teams, trust, and the part that is not code. On the agenda the talks are grouped into three tracks: AI, Open Source and Humans.

items.q: How can I become a speaker?
items.a: The Call for Proposals closed over the summer and the program for DevFest.cz 2026 is out — see the speakers and agenda pages. For any speaker enquiries, reach us at devfest-speakers@gug.cz.

items.q: What's the story with the detective theme?
items.a: This year's edition is styled as a film-noir case, and the case doesn't stay on the posters: there's a game running through the day for anyone who wants to play investigator. More is revealed closer to the date — and on the day itself.

items.q: I'm coming — how do I tell people?
items.a: Make a share card on the I'm attending page: add your photo (processed on your device only) or let your initials carry it, then download it or share it straight to your feed.

items.q: How can my company become a partner?
items.a: See the Partners page for what we offer, or write to filip@gug.cz.
Drop your email in the form on the home page and follow us on social media — ticket drops and program news land there first.
